annotations.description: The player chose to mulligan a 7-card hand that had 2 Plains, multiple white creatures including a 1-drop (Infantry Veteran), a 2-drop (Daybreak Charger), a combat trick (Moment of Triumph), and powerful late-game cards (Blessed Sanctuary, Knight of the Tusk). While the hand only has 2 lands, both are Plains which cast all the early plays. This is a keepable hand - it has a strong curve if it draws a third land, and even without one it can deploy Infantry Veteran turn 1 and Daybreak Charger turn 2. Mulliganing to 6 loses a card for no good reason.
annotations.actionTaken: Mulliganed a 7-card hand with 2 Plains, a 1-drop, a 2-drop, a combat trick, and strong late-game cards.
annotations.betterLine: Keep the 7-card hand. It has a playable curve starting turn 1 with Infantry Veteran, turn 2 Daybreak Charger, and just needs to draw one more land for the mid-game plays. Two lands with low-curve spells is a reasonable keep.

annotations.description: Playing Forest turn 1 instead of Treetop Village. Since there's nothing to cast turn 1 and Treetop Village enters tapped, playing it now costs nothing while saving a future turn's tempo. The player has no 1-mana plays, so the tapped land is free on turn 1.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest on turn 1
annotations.betterLine: Play Treetop Village turn 1 (enters tapped for free since no T1 plays), then Swamp turn 2 for Oathsworn Vampire, Forest turn 3 for Uktabi Orangutan.

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Swamp means GPT5n Perfect cannot cast anything this turn. Playing Swamp would give Forest + Swamp = {1}{B}, allowing Oathsworn Vampire to be cast this turn as a 2/2 creature. Missing a turn of development when the opponent also has limited board presence.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest, leaving no castable spells this turn.
annotations.betterLine: Play Swamp, then cast Oathsworn Vampire ({1}{B}) to develop the board. Oathsworn Vampire enters tapped so it wouldn't block anyway, but getting it down a turn earlier is meaningful tempo.

annotations.description: Chose Oathsworn Vampire (enters tapped, 2/2) over Uktabi Orangutan (2/2, enters untapped and can block immediately). The remaining 2 mana from casting Vampire has no useful purpose this turn since there's nothing in hand that costs 2 or less. Orangutan's ETB is wasted (no artifacts), but the untapped body is more immediately useful for blocking. Vampire's graveyard recursion is long-term upside, but playing the Orangutan now and saving the Vampire for a turn where its recursion or the tap drawback matters less could be better.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Oathsworn Vampire, leaving 2 mana unused with no way to spend it
annotations.betterLine: Cast Uktabi Orangutan as the 2/2 that enters untapped and can immediately block, saving Oathsworn Vampire for later when its graveyard recursion is relevant

annotations.description: Failed to attack with Angelic Cub 1/1 when the opponent had no untapped creatures to block and no mana available. This was a free point of damage with zero risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and did not declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Angelic Cub for 1 free damage, then play Plains and cast Taranika, Akroan Veteran in the post-combat main phase.

annotations.description: Played Forest instead of Treetop Village. Both allow casting Uktabi Orangutan this turn (2 Forest + 1 Swamp = 3 mana including G), but Treetop Village provides a creature-land for future turns, which is strictly more valuable than a basic Forest.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest as the land drop
annotations.betterLine: Play Treetop Village (enters tapped but still have 3 untapped mana to cast Uktabi Orangutan, and gain access to a 3/3 trample creature-land in future turns)

annotations.description: Playing Forest instead of Treetop Village in postcombat main phase. Playing Forest now wastes the opportunity to 'hide' the tapped entry cost of Treetop Village.
annotations.actionTaken: Played Forest
annotations.betterLine: Play Treetop Village, which enters tapped but costs nothing this turn since it's postcombat. This preserves untapped land plays (Forest/Swamp) for future turns when immediate mana matters more.

annotations.description: Sonnet Trash failed to attack with Angelic Cub (a 2/2) when the opponent's only untapped creature is sick (Uktabi Orangutan just entered) and the Oathsworn Vampire is tapped. annotations.actionTaken: Timed out and didn't declare any attackers.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Angelic Cub for 2 unblocked damage, bringing the opponent to 14 life.

annotations.description: Failed to block Oathsworn Vampire 2/2 with Taranika 3/3. Taranika would survive the block, kill the vampire (which has graveyard recursion potential), and save 2 life. The timeout/no response meant taking unnecessary damage and leaving the vampire alive.

annotations.description: Attempted to cast Hooting Mandrills before playing a land, resulting in a failed cast (rolled back by game engine).
